The paper does not describe any CRISPRi system being used in *S. marcescens* — in fact, it reports the opposite: among the remaining limitations of the genetic toolbox, "regulatory tools such as CRISPRi and CRISPRa are lacking" (p. 8).

What *is* described for handling competing pathways is gene deletion/knockout and related strategies, not CRISPRi, for example:

- CRISPR-Cas9 is available in *S. marcescens* as a genome-editing (not interference) tool: Gou et al.'s dual-plasmid CRISPR-Cas9 system driven by a stationary-phase promoter, enabling gene deletion, targeted integration and single-nucleotide mutagenesis with efficiencies >80% (p. 7).
- Deletion of competing pathway genes, e.g. *budC* in strain G12 to block acetoin→2,3-BD conversion (pp. 9–10), *slaC* deletion in MG1 (p. 10), deletion of by-product pathways (lactate, acetate, ethanol) and modulation of global regulators (*arcA*, *iclR*) in HBQA7 (p. 11), *phoA* deletion for (−)-α-bisabolol (p. 11), and *speG* deletion for spermidine production (p. 11).

So, on the evidence in this review, no CRISPRi system has been applied in this organism.
question: Which CRISPRi system was used to repress competing pathways in S. marcescens?
